title: A reviewed average-output domination condition earns a nonstationary hold bound
statement: Let the actual stationary rho, decoded Q_j and bad projector P satisfy [H,Q_j](I-P)=0, ||[H,Q_j]||<=c_j and p=Tr(rho P). A writer W with W(I/2)<=kappa rho and initial decoded diamond error epsilon_write earns reference-safe storage error <=min(2,epsilon_write+2 kappa p T sum_j c_j), at most epsilon_write+12 kappa v_dyn n p T when c_j<=2 v_dyn n. Hermiticity gives two-sided P support; every written marginal <=2 kappa rho stays dominated by stationarity. A Gibbs-preserving terminal channel has kappa_N=1, but logical fidelity is separate. The ideal Petz embedding W_rho(X)=sqrt(rho)(r^-1/2 X r^-1/2 tensor I)sqrt(rho), r=Tr_G rho, is CPTP, obeys W(r)=rho and has kappa=1/[2 lambda_min(r)]. For delta=||rho-I/2 tensor Tr_L rho||_1<1, kappa<=1/(1-delta) and epsilon_write<=min(2,2[sqrt(2delta/(1-delta))+(1-delta)^-1/2-1]). This familiar ideal global map is not a physical writer or novelty claim. Independent thermal-bit flips require kappa_N>=(p'/p)^n even with an exactly identity logical channel. Thus small local stochastic faults, mean energy or accurate decoding do not imply volume-independent domination. Thermal information, coherence, switching/reset work and low-temperature polarization remain charged.
